title: CV
text:
My CV and this website draw on one spreadsheet of publications, presentations and other entries. The CV is typeset from it with R and the vitae package, which keeps maintaining the record separate from formatting it. This site is built from the same spreadsheet with R and Quarto: only the entries marked for the website are published, and each rebuild updates the publication and talk archives.

  
    Download the CV (PDF, 164 KB)
  
  Last updated: 27 October 2026

title: About
text: I am training as a physician-scientist on a combined MD/PhD path. My current work is my doctoral research, as an NIH Oxford–Cambridge Scholar based in Cambridge, UK, alongside national climate-health leadership.

title: About
text:
Current work
Research. My doctoral project combines experimental virology, epidemiology and evolutionary modelling, in two strands. In one, I develop phylodynamic methods to estimate differences in fitness among co-circulating dengue lineages. In the other, I test how temperature may affect viral stability and fitness.
Climate and health. As National Chair of Medical Students for a Sustainable Future, I help translate climate-health evidence into education, communication and action across health-professional networks.

title: About
text:
Direction
The thread through this work is translation across scales: from a virus and a model to patients, institutions, communities and public-health action. My medical and research training are preparing me to work as a physician-scientist for public health; that is where my training is heading, not a role I already hold.

title: Douglas Fritz
text:
Douglas Fritz
    Translational physician-scientist for public health
    MD/PhD researcher and NIH Oxford–Cambridge Scholar, based in Cambridge, UK
  
  


I work at the intersection of climate change, infectious disease, medicine and health-professional education. My doctoral research combines experimental virology, epidemiology and evolutionary modelling, and I help translate climate-health evidence into education, communication and action across health-professional networks.

title: Research
text:
Douglas Fritz’s work sits under one umbrella identity: translational physician-scientist for public health. It is not a research area of its own. It describes how four research pillars relate: scientific questions, the methods used to answer them, their application to patients and health systems, and the perspective of climate and planetary health.
Each pillar below has its role, the questions it includes, topic tags from its publications and talks, up to three selected outputs, and links to the publication and talk archives filtered to that pillar. The counts come from the same public records that the archives list.

title: Research
text:
How the pillars connect
The pillars are aids for navigation and interpretation, not mutually exclusive academic departments. Every publication and talk has one primary pillar and may have a secondary one, so the same work can be reached from two pillars; selected outputs that come from a secondary pillar are marked “also tagged”. Read together, Pillar 1 holds the core scientific questions, Pillar 2 the methods and discovery practice used to answer them, Pillar 3 their application to patients and health systems, and Pillar 4 the perspective, values and applied field of climate and planetary health in medicine.
